Topics · The holy books together

How does the Quran honour Mary?

Mary is the one woman the Quran names. Chosen above the women of the worlds, a model for all who believe.

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَإِذْ قَالَتِ ٱلْمَلَـٰٓئِكَةُ يَـٰمَرْيَمُ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱصْطَفَىٰكِ وَطَهَّرَكِ وَٱصْطَفَىٰكِ عَلَىٰ نِسَآءِ ٱلْعَـٰلَمِينَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And [mention] when the angels said, "O Mary, indeed Allāh has chosen you and purified you and chosen you above the women of the worlds.

Quran · Aal Imran 3:42

Translation

Having come in, the angel said to her, “Rejoice, you highly favored one! The Lord is with you. Blessed are you among women!” But when she saw him, she was greatly troubled at the saying, and considered what kind of salutation this might be. The angel said to her, “Don’t be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ εἰσελθὼν πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Χαῖρε, κεχαριτωμένη, ὁ κύριος μετὰ σοῦ. ἡ δὲ ἐπὶ τῷ λόγῳ διεταράχθη καὶ διελογίζετο ποταπὸς εἴη ὁ ἀσπασμὸς οὗτος. καὶ εἶπεν ὁ ἄγγελος αὐτῇ· Μὴ φοβοῦ, Μαριάμ, εὗρες γὰρ χάριν παρὰ τῷ θεῷ·

the Gospel (Luke) · 1:28-30

World English Bible

This surprises many people. Of all the women in the Quran, one alone is called by her name, and that is Mary, thirty-four times, with a whole chapter that bears her name. In the verse angels tell her she has been chosen, purified, and chosen above the women of the worlds. Whatever you believe, you can weigh this: a book that came six centuries after her, from another land and in another language, gives her the highest place it gives any woman.

A question for you

What surprises you most here?

If you sayThat the Quran honours her at all
ThenThen you were expecting distance, or rivalry. The verse leaves no room for that. Ask why a book like this would give her so much.
If you sayThat she alone is mentioned by name
ThenThat makes her name a kind of mark in the Quran. Every other woman there is known by her tie to someone: the wife of one, the mother of another. She is Mary.
If you sayThat she stands above the women of the worlds
ThenThat is a sentence about her own standing before God. It rests on no community's claim to her.

Part 2 of 4

﴿فَأَجَآءَهَا ٱلْمَخَاضُ إِلَىٰ جِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ قَالَتْ يَـٰلَيْتَنِى مِتُّ قَبْلَ هَـٰذَا وَكُنتُ نَسْيًا مَّنسِيًّا٢٣ فَنَادَىٰهَا مِن تَحْتِهَآ أَلَّا تَحْزَنِى قَدْ جَعَلَ رَبُّكِ تَحْتَكِ سَرِيًّا٢٤ وَهُزِّىٓ إِلَيْكِ بِجِذْعِ ٱلنَّخْلَةِ تُسَـٰقِطْ عَلَيْكِ رُطَبًا جَنِيًّا٢٥﴾

Translation of the meaning

And the pains of childbirth drove her to the trunk of a palm tree. She said, "Oh, I wish I had died before this and was in oblivion, forgotten." But he[812] called her from below her, "Do not grieve; your Lord has provided beneath you a stream. And shake toward you the trunk of the palm tree; it will drop upon you ripe, fresh dates.

Translator's notes

[812] There is a difference of opinion among scholars as to whether "he" refers to the baby or to the angel.

Quran · Maryam 19:23-25

Honour here does not mean a life without pain. The verses place her alone at the trunk of a palm tree, in labour, wishing she had died before this and been forgotten. The Quran keeps her words. Then a voice tells her not to grieve: water below her, ripe dates from the tree. Remove her fear and her courage goes with it. The honour here belongs to a woman who went through all of this, with God beside her in it.

A question for you

Which picture of Mary is closest to the one you know?

If you sayThe honoured mother, crowned in heaven
ThenMany Christians love her this way, and that love has lasted centuries. The Quran shows her holding on to a palm tree, with God caring for her. You may find the two meet.
If you sayThe young woman who said yes
ThenThe Quran's Mary is afraid, asks how, and comes to believe the words of her Lord. The word it uses for her comes next.
If you sayThe sorrowing mother at the cross
ThenMany have known that sorrow. These verses show her in another hour of fear, alone, and cared for.
If you sayI know little about her
ThenThen you are meeting her here for the first time: alone, afraid, and kept safe. That is a good place to start.

Part 3 of 4

﴿مَّا ٱلْمَسِيحُ ٱبْنُ مَرْيَمَ إِلَّا رَسُولٌ قَدْ خَلَتْ مِن قَبْلِهِ ٱلرُّسُلُ وَأُمُّهُۥ صِدِّيقَةٌ ۖ كَانَا يَأْكُلَانِ ٱلطَّعَامَ ۗ ٱنظُرْ كَيْفَ نُبَيِّنُ لَهُمُ ٱلْـَٔايَـٰتِ ثُمَّ ٱنظُرْ أَنَّىٰ يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾

Translation of the meaning

The Messiah, son of Mary, was not but a messenger; [other] messengers have passed on before him. And his mother was a supporter of truth. They both used to eat food.[277] Look how We make clear to them the signs; then look how they are deluded.

Translator's notes

[277] They were in need of sustenance, proving that they were creations of Allāh, not divine beings.

Quran · Al-Ma'idah 5:75

Translation

The multitudes said, “This is the prophet, Jesus, from Nazareth of Galilee.”

Original · Ancient Greek

οἱ δὲ ὄχλοι ἔλεγον· Οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ προφήτης Ἰησοῦς ὁ ἀπὸ Ναζαρὲθ τῆς Γαλιλαίας.

the Gospel (Matthew) · 21:11

World English Bible

The Quran gives Mary the title siddiqa, a woman of truth, whose whole life agrees with what she believed. In the same sentence it says she and her son ate food. That can sound like a slight. In the Quran it draws a line: the highest honour a creature can have, and nothing beyond it, since whoever eats depends on the One who feeds. Many who love Mary say they do not worship her, and on her this line does not oppose them.

A question for you

What do you think this description leaves room for?

If you sayHonour, love, and asking for her prayers
ThenHonour and love stand firm in the verse. On calling to someone unseen the Quran has more to say, in the Step on speaking to God directly. Readers differ on this.
If you sayFor her to be a model, and that is enough
ThenThen you honour her by walking as she walked. The next verse takes that further than you might expect.
If you sayIt feels too small for her
ThenMany who love her would say so. Take that feeling to the next verse, where the Quran lifts her up as an example to everyone who believes.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَضَرَبَ ٱللَّهُ مَثَلًا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ ٱمْرَأَتَ فِرْعَوْنَ إِذْ قَالَتْ رَبِّ ٱبْنِ لِى عِندَكَ بَيْتًا فِى ٱلْجَنَّةِ وَنَجِّنِى مِن فِرْعَوْنَ وَعَمَلِهِۦ وَنَجِّنِى مِنَ ٱلْقَوْمِ ٱلظَّـٰلِمِينَ١١ وَمَرْيَمَ ٱبْنَتَ عِمْرَٰنَ ٱلَّتِىٓ أَحْصَنَتْ فَرْجَهَا فَنَفَخْنَا فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِنَا وَصَدَّقَتْ بِكَلِمَـٰتِ رَبِّهَا وَكُتُبِهِۦ وَكَانَتْ مِنَ ٱلْقَـٰنِتِينَ١٢﴾

Translation of the meaning

And Allāh presents an example of those who believed: the wife of Pharaoh, when she said, "My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds and save me from the wrongdoing people." And [the example of] Mary, the daughter of ʿImrān, who guarded her chastity, so We blew into [her garment] through Our angel [i.e., Gabriel], and she believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures and was of the devoutly obedient.

Quran · At-Tahrim 66:11-12

Translation

and she had been a widow for about eighty-four years), who didn’t depart from the temple, worshiping with fastings and petitions night and day.

Original · Ancient Greek

καὶ αὐτὴ χήρα ἕως ἐτῶν ὀγδοήκοντα τεσσάρων,) ἣ οὐκ ἀφίστατο τοῦ ἱεροῦ νηστείαις καὶ δεήσεσιν λατρεύουσα νύκτα καὶ ἡμέραν.

the Gospel (Luke) · 2:37

World English Bible

The last mention goes further. The Quran sets out an example for everyone who believes, men and women alike, and chooses two women: the wife of Pharaoh, and Mary. Of Mary it says she kept herself chaste, she believed the words of her Lord and His books, and she was among the devoted. Anyone who assumes that examples of faith must be men may want to read this twice. A woman is the model for the men reading too.

A question for you

Which of her qualities would you most want in your own life?

If you sayHer trust in what she could not understand
ThenThat is the word she believed. It begins where what you can see runs out.
If you sayHer courage when alone
ThenShe walked away from everyone, then carried her son back to her people. The verses see her in both.
If you sayHer faithfulness on ordinary days
ThenThat is the meaning of the devout word: quiet, lasting obedience. No one writes about it. The Quran did.

The same in the other books
